blocks.text: After the structure of DNA was discovered (1953) and the central dogma proposed (1957), biologists asked how DNA, with only four kinds of nucleotide, could store the information for thousands of different proteins, what the nature of the genetic code was, and how the order of nucleotides could specify the order of amino acids.

In 1961 Crick and his colleagues proposed that the genetic code is a series of blocks of information called codons, each specifying one amino acid. One nucleotide per amino acid could code only 4 amino acids, and two nucleotides only 16 (4 x 4), so a codon must be three nucleotides: 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 combinations, more than enough for 20 amino acids. The code is therefore a triplet code.

When a gene works, the codons on the DNA are transcribed into complementary codons of mRNA, so the DNA triplet TAC becomes the mRNA codon AUG. 'Codon' usually means the mRNA codon, but it is sometimes used for DNA triplets, especially when discussing mutations.
Work of Nirenberg, Leder and Khorana

In 1961 the American biochemist Marshall Nirenberg made a poly-U mRNA, of uracil nucleotides only, and added it to bacterial cytoplasm; a polypeptide of many phenylalanines was made, so UUU specifies phenylalanine. Nirenberg and the American geneticist Philip Leder tested triplets and assigned amino acids to 47 codons; Har Gobind Khorana, who completed his studies at Government College, Lahore, determined the remaining 17.

items: Of the 64 codons, UGA, UAG and UAA are stop (nonsense) codons: they specify no amino acid and end protein synthesis.
AUG is the start codon at the beginning of genes; it specifies methionine.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: The information in DNA for making proteins is the genetic code, a series of three-nucleotide codons. The 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Nirenberg (the genetic code), Khorana (synthesis of nucleic acids) and Robert Holley (the chemical structure of transfer RNA).

blocks.prompt: If a DNA template triplet is AAA, what is the mRNA codon and the amino acid?
blocks.explanation: The mRNA codon is UUU, which codes for phenylalanine (Nirenberg's poly-U result).

items: Crick (1961): triplet codons; 64 codons for 20 amino acids.
Nirenberg: UUU = phenylalanine; Nirenberg and Leder 47 codons, Khorana 17.
AUG start (Met); UAA, UAG, UGA stop.
